title: Emit model metadata change events from control plane
author: Michael Nguyen
release_notes: Internal: Control plane now emits structured model metadata change + promotion events for changelog generation and rollout auditability.
No customer-facing behavior change yet (events are consumed by internal generator + Console).
description: Context: The model metadata schema v1 work (registry + validation) needs a single, reliable stream of change events to drive the changelog generator and Console "change history" views. Today we have ad-hoc logging and some release-engineering notes, but not an auditable, machine-consumable event source. This PR introduces a canonical event envelope and emits two primary event types from the control plane whenever (a) model metadata is updated, and (b) a model version is promoted within an environment/deployment scope (Hosted/Dedicated/Private). It also implements idempotency + dedupe so consumers can safely replay. Summary of changes: 1) New event types and schema (v1): - redwood.model_registry.model_metadata_changed.v1 - redwood.model_registry.model_version_promoted.v1 Event envelope fields are consistent with our other platform events: event_id (UUID), occurred_at, emitted_at, actor (service/user), request_id, environment (prod/staging), and payload. Payload includes model_id, model_slug, variant_id (where applicable), metadata_schema_version, metadata_hash, and redaction_scope (public/internal). For promotion events, payload also includes from_version, to_version, rollout_policy_id (nullable), and deployment_scope (hosted|dedicated|private) + region (nullable). 2) Outbox-based delivery with deterministic idempotency keys: We write events into a control-plane outbox table in the same DB transaction as the metadata update/promotion (so we don't emit an event without the change). A background worker publishes to Event Bus (Kafka) and marks rows delivered. We compute a stable idempotency_key per event to prevent duplicates across retries and replays: - model_metadata_changed: sha256("model_metadata_changed:v1" + model_id + metadata_hash + public_or_internal + updated_at_rfc3339) - model_version_promoted: sha256("model_version_promoted:v1" + model_id + deployment_scope + region_or_all + to_version + promotion_id) This makes the publisher and downstream consumers (generator/Console) safe under at-least-once semantics. 3) Public vs internal separation: Events are emitted in two flavors when needed: a public event (public payload only) and an internal event (includes internal-only notes / eval references / operational details). The default bus topic is internal; public event forwarding is gated behind the changelog generator’s redaction filter and will be handled in the generator PR (see linked work). This PR ensures payloads are explicitly tagged with redaction_scope, and tests assert that public payloads never include internal_notes, jira_links, incident_refs, or raw eval artifacts. 4) Promotion semantics: Promotion events are emitted only when the "active" version pointer changes for a given scope (model+deployment_scope+region). Metadata edits that do not change the active version do not emit promotion events (only metadata_changed). Promotions caused by rollback emit the same event type with from_version/to_version swapped; the payload includes promotion_reason (manual|rollback|policy). 5) Observability + guardrails: - Metrics: control_plane_outbox_publish_total{event_type,status}, control_plane_outbox_backlog, control_plane_event_publish_latency_ms - Logging includes event_id, idempotency_key, request_id, and actor_id. - Feature flag: model_metadata_events_v1 enabled in staging by default; prod ramp via config. Notes for reviewers: - Event schema is defined in control-plane events module (protobuf-style struct + JSON serialization). The generator will consume JSON. We intentionally versioned the event name with .v1 to allow non-breaking schema evolution via .v2 later. - Some fields are currently nullable (rollout_policy_id, region) since not all promotion paths have that info yet. We should consider requiring rollout_policy_id once rollouts are fully wired (tracked in ENG-9823 follow-up). Related: - Depends on metadata hash computed by registry schema v1 (see redwood-model-registry PR #18421). - Migration/backfill PR #18429 will generate a small burst of metadata_changed events during backfill; this PR includes a backfill_suppression flag for the migration job to avoid spamming downstream consumers (default true for backfill job). Test plan: - Unit tests for idempotency_key stability and public/internal payload redaction - Integration test: metadata update transaction writes outbox row and publisher sends exactly once under retry - Integration test: promotion emits exactly one event per scope and is deduped across double-submit - Load test (staging): 10k events replay through publisher; no duplicate consumer processing when using idempotency_key as dedupe key. Rollout: - Land behind feature flag - Enable in staging (24h) and validate generator ingestion metrics - Enable in prod at 10%, 50%, 100% over 2 days; monitor outbox backlog and publish failures
commits: control-plane/events: add model_registry event envelope + payload definitions
control-plane/model-registry: emit metadata_changed events on create/update
control-plane/rollouts: emit version_promoted event on active pointer change
control-plane/outbox: add idempotency_key + unique index and publisher retries
tests: redaction + idempotency + promotion semantics coverage
ops: add metrics + dashboards hooks for event publish pipeline
review_conversation: Logan Wright: Can we guarantee ordering between metadata_changed and version_promoted for the same request? Some consumers may assume metadata is available when they see promotion.

Michael Nguyen (author): Yes for same request/transaction: we enqueue both events in the same outbox transaction and publish in insertion order. Added a comment + integration test asserting ordering for combined update+promotion path.
Jordan Lee: Promotion payload should include deployment_scope + region; also need an explicit promotion_reason for rollback to avoid confusing changelog templates.
Michael Nguyen (author): Added deployment_scope/region (nullable region) and promotion_reason enum (manual|rollback|policy). Updated docs + tests.
Quentin Harris: Please ensure public events never include internal_notes or eval_run_ids. I’m worried about accidental leakage via "debug" fields.
Michael Nguyen (author): Public payload builder now uses an allowlist transform (not a denylist). Added tests that snapshot public JSON and fail if forbidden keys appear.
Chloe Martin: Console will filter by deployment/region; can you include a stable scope_key so we can index quickly without re-deriving it client-side?
Michael Nguyen (author): Added scope_key = "{model_id}:{deployment_scope}:{region|all}" and documented it as a derived, stable field (not a primary identifier).
Ethan Park: Outbox unique constraint on idempotency_key looks good. Make sure retry logic treats 409/duplicate as success and advances the cursor.
Michael Nguyen (author): Updated publisher to treat unique violation as delivered (idempotent) and continue; added unit test.
